text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) electron gain enthalpy
(2) the modern periodic law
(3) ionisation enthalpy
(4) electronegativity
Column B
(a) The energy needed to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
(b) The energy change when an isolated gaseous atom gains an electron.
(c) An atom’s tendency to attract a shared pair of electrons to itself.
(d) Properties of the elements repeat periodically with increasing atomic number.

points.text: (1) electron gain enthalpy goes with (b).
(2) the modern periodic law goes with (d).
(3) ionisation enthalpy goes with (a).
(4) electronegativity goes with (c).

subject: chemistry
facts: c11-3a:Arrange in increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy
text: Arrange in increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy: Mg, Na, Al.

points.text: Na, Al, Mg
Na is lowest. Mg is above Al, because its full 3s² subshell is more stable than aluminium’s single 3p electron.
